Pfizer's latest filing says it expects total net cost savings of about $6.7 billion from the program through 2029. That is up from about $5.7 billion through 2026 (about $5.1 billion achieved through 2025 and $600 million still expected by the end of 2026). The extra $1.0 billion comes with about $2.0 billion of one-time costs to achieve it. The filings name the program "Realigning Our Cost Base Program", which I treated as the "Cost Realignment Program" you asked about.
In its FY2025 10-K, Pfizer said the Realigning Our Cost Base Program was expected to deliver total net cost savings of approximately $5.7 billion through 2026. That was made up of $5.1 billion achieved through 2025 and the remaining anticipated savings of $600 million, primarily in SI&A, expected by the end of 2026.
In its Q2 2026 10-Q, Pfizer said it announced $1.0 billion of additional anticipated net cost savings for the program. It now expects total net cost savings of approximately $6.7 billion from the program through 2029.
Pfizer expects one-time costs to achieve the additional savings to be incurred through 2029 and to total approximately $2.0 billion.
